methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $8.6B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.8B - $39.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Wayve, a Series D AI & Software company, is valued at $8.6B post-money and has raised $1.5B to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable (Palantir, ticker PLTR), all operating in frontier AI and autonomous systems software.

Two methods anchor the valuation range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, implying $12.9B. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies yields $10.0B, with the peer set ranging from $3.8B (Ayar Labs, Series E) to $39.0B (Figure AI, Series C). The wide peer dispersion—spanning more than a 10x range—reflects heterogeneous market valuations within early-stage frontier AI.

The triangulated range sits at $8.5B (low) to $14.8B (high), with a median of $11.4B. Wayve's current valuation of $8.6B aligns with the lower bound, consistent with its position as a Series D company relative to later-stage peers in the comp set. Key uncertainties include capital intensity of deployment, competitive positioning relative to Figure AI's outlier valuation, and stage-specific risk premia in autonomous systems software. The narrow two-method basis limits conviction; broader applicability of revenue or operational metrics would strengthen the analysis.
